newsitem.title: CHINA: China policeman sentenced to death in graft case.
newsitem.headline: China policeman sentenced to death in graft case.

text.p: A court in northeastern China has sentenced to death a senior police officer for embezzling 20.19 million yuan ($2.43 million) in what a regional newspaper described as China's biggest police corruption case.

The Intermediate People's Court in Jinzhou in Liaoning province recently convicted Zhao Guoli, former deputy chief of the public security bureau of the local economic development zone, of abusing his powers for personal benefit, the Nanjing Evening News Weekend newspaper reported.
The newspaper, available in Beijing on Monday, said the court sentenced Zhao to death and he had appealed.
It described the case as the biggest corruption case involving a police officer since the 1949 communist takeover.

In addition to being deputy head of the zone's public security bureau, Zhao headed a company owned by the bureau and used the company to juggle numerous invoices, embezzling 20.19 millon yuan in 250 days, the newspaper quoted the court as saying.
Public security bureaux in China are not allowed to operate companies.
Zhao had informed against a senior Jinzhou port official in a bid to win leniency from the court, the newspaper said.
The Supreme People's Court in Liaoning province would hear his appeal soon, a local court official said by telephone, but declined to give further details.

China's market-oriented economic reforms have created unprecedented opportunities for officials to abuse their positions for personal gain, and President Jiang Zemin has repeatedly warned that corruption is the most serious threat to the power of the ruling Communist Party.
